text: Half mad with fear, I rushed into the great hall, where the little people were sleeping, and woke them by shouting and striking a match. <break time="0.8s" /> A few of them laughed, but most of them looked terribly frightened, and they ran away from me into the darkness. <break time="0.8s" /> Exhausted at last, I fell asleep on the ground near the sphinx, and when I woke up, it was already morning. <break time="0.8s" /> In the calm light of day I could think clearly, and I knew that the machine could not have traveled in time without its levers. <break time="0.8s" /> Then I found a groove torn in the grass, with strange narrow footprints beside it, which led straight to the bronze pedestal of the sphinx. <break time="0.8s" /> The pedestal had panels of bronze on its sides, but there were no handles or keyholes, and the panels would not move at all. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked the little people by signs to open the panels, they turned away from me as if I had done something shameful. <break time="0.8s" /> Patience, I told myself, for the only way to get my machine back was to learn the secrets of this strange world. <break time="0.8s" /> A few days later I saved a little girl named Weena from drowning, and from then on she followed me everywhere like a gentle friend.
